$comment: Accepted npm audit advisories (m1-009). Checked by scripts/audit-check.mjs in CI. One entry per advisory (GHSA ID). For high and critical advisories, `affects` lists every package npm flagged through that advisory when it was accepted; a new package means a new dependency path and fails CI. reviewBy is at most maxReviewDays after accepted; an expired entry fails CI until it is re-decided. Re-decided under D-M0-5 (S5/S6) in m1-011 (2026-10-20): all three re-accepted unchanged, see `reviewed`. Never use `npm audit fix --force`: it would downgrade apostrophe to 3.x and nodemon to 1.x.
auditSummary: 43 package findings (38 moderate, 5 high, 0 critical) from 3 advisories (1 high, 2 moderate). Production-only (--omit=dev): 42 findings, 4 high.

advisories.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
advisories.scope: prod (apostrophe -> chokidar -> braces; nunjucks also lists chokidar) and dev (nodemon -> chokidar -> braces)
advisories.reason: No braces release outside the affected range (<=3.0.3) is available to this tree; npm's only fix is a semver-major downgrade of apostrophe (to 3.x) and nodemon (to 1.x). apostrophe uses chokidar to watch view and asset directories during development; the watched glob patterns come from the application, not from visitors. nodemon runs on developer machines only.
advisories.remediation: m1-011: no patched braces release exists (first_patched_version null). chokidar 4+ drops braces, but apostrophe and nunjucks require chokidar ^3 and use glob watching, so an npm override would be a semver-major change to core internals: rejected. Watch paths are application-controlled and chokidar watching is a development feature. Re-check at the next apostrophe release or by reviewBy.

advisories.title: Tiptap: mergeAttributes() turns an own __proto__ key into inherited executable DOM attributes
advisories.scope: prod (apostrophe rich-text editor, admin UI only)
advisories.reason: apostrophe 4.34.0 depends on Tiptap 2.x (@tiptap/starter-kit ^2.27.2) for the rich-text editor, which only logged-in editors load. The advisory is fixed in Tiptap 3.30.4, outside apostrophe's supported range.
advisories.remediation: m1-011: apostrophe 4.34.0 still ships Tiptap 2.27.3; fixed only in Tiptap 3.30.4+, outside core's range. Exposure is limited to logged-in editors (rich-text editor). Upgrade when an apostrophe release moves to Tiptap 3; editor access reviewed under D-M0-11.

advisories.title: sprintf-js vulnerable to denial of service through unbounded precision specifiers
advisories.reason: Reached through underscore.string inside apostrophe core; format strings come from code, not from visitors. No compatible fixed release in this tree.
advisories.remediation: m1-011: no patched sprintf-js release exists (first_patched_version null). Reached through underscore.string in core with code-supplied format strings. Re-check at the next apostrophe release or by reviewBy.

reviewed.result: npm audit unchanged: 43 findings (38 moderate, 5 high, 0 critical) from the same 3 advisories; production-only 42 (4 high). apostrophe 4.34.0, @apostrophecms/form 1.5.6 and db-connect 1.1.0 are the latest releases. No apostrophe advisory affects 4.34.0. No compatible fix exists for any of the three (GitHub advisory API: braces and sprintf-js have no patched version; Tiptap is fixed only in 3.30.4+).
